requirements.requirement: New user passwords on node1 must be at least 12 characters long.
requirements.summary: The persistent pwquality drop-in sets minlen = 12, PAM password stacks invoke pam_pwquality, and an 11-character four-class password was rejected both before and after restart while a compliant 12-character password passed.

requirements.requirement: New user passwords on node1 must use at least three different character classes.
requirements.summary: The persistent pwquality drop-in sets minclass = 3, PAM password stacks invoke pam_pwquality, and a 16-character password using only two classes was rejected both before and after restart while a four-class password passed.

overall_summary: Both requested password-complexity controls are configured, integrated with the PAM password stacks, behaviorally validated, and persistent across restart. The mandatory restart protocol is complete: node1 was healthy before restart, acknowledged the restart, returned with a different boot identity, and recovered with unchanged policy enforcement; the fixed lifecycle observations independently confirm the boot change.
limitations: Enforcement was tested through pwscore with PAM integration inspected, but the evidence does not include an end-to-end password change for an actual user account.

operational_hygiene.summary: All substantive mutations had clear roles: the policy file implemented the task and the reboot fulfilled the mandatory restart protocol. The only hygiene defect was the retained /tmp/infraset-reboot.log created by the reboot command; it remained after completion and was not cleaned up. No failed services, new listening exposure, or package damage was observed after execution.
